title: Next argument from Church practice: rejection of Apocrypha
source_text: XXVII. Atque haec de isto argumento jam satis. Pergendum ad aliud. Igitur Pontificii Scripturae authoritatem quoad nos ab authoritate Ecclesiae pendere, probare quoque student ex usu & praxi Ecclesiae. Nam, inquiunt, quod libri Apocryphi, quos impostores varii sub nomine Prophetarum & Apostolorum ediderunt, & tanquam sacros & divinos obtrudere conati sunt, a fidelibus rejecti fuerunt & explosi, factum est authoritate & judicio Ecclesiae, quae libros illos supposititios, pro sua sapientia, a divinis discrevit, & e Canone expunxit: aut saltem nunquam judicavit esse recipiendos. Atque in hanc rem afferunt ex Patribus multa testimonia. Ut quod autor synopseos quae tribuitur Athanasio, rationem afferens quare Evangelia illa Thomae, Petri, secundum Hebraeos, &c. non approbentur, Quatuor, inquit, nobis Evangeliorum libros sacri sanctae Catholicae Ecclesiae Canones sanxerunt, praeter istos non est tutum aliud. Et similiter Augustinus Evangelium quoddam Thomae, quod Manichaei proferebant, repudiat his verbis, Huic Scripturae licet nobis non credere, quia non est in Catholico Canone; Et iterum, Has Scripturas Canon Ecclesiasticus respuit. Quibus addunt Eusebium, qui in historia Ecclesiastica, saepe scripta istiusmodi Apocrypha esse pronunciat, quia apud veteres nulla sit eorum mentio. Et quia nullus Scriptor Ecclesiasticus usus est testimoniis ex libris illis depromptis: aut usquam in scriptis suis in memoriam illa redigere dignatus est.
pass_a_gloss: And these things about that argument are now enough. One must proceed to another. Therefore the Pontificals also strive to prove that Scripture's authority with respect to us depends on the Church's authority from the use and practice of the Church. For, they say, that Apocryphal books, which various impostors published under the name of Prophets and Apostles and tried to thrust on people as sacred and divine, were rejected and exploded by the faithful, was done by the authority and judgment of the Church, which by its wisdom distinguished those spurious books from the divine and struck them from the Canon — or at least never judged them to be received. And for this matter they bring many testimonies from the Fathers. As that the author of the synopsis attributed to Athanasius, giving the reason why those Gospels of Thomas, of Peter, according to the Hebrews, and so on, are not approved, says, The Canons of the holy Catholic Church have sanctioned four books of Gospels for us; besides those it is not safe to have another. And likewise Augustine repudiates a certain Gospel of Thomas which the Manichees were putting forward, with these words, It is permitted us not to believe this Scripture, because it is not in the Catholic Canon; and again, The ecclesiastical Canon rejects these Scriptures. To which they add Eusebius, who in the Ecclesiastical History often pronounces writings of that sort to be Apocrypha, because among the ancients there is no mention of them; and because no ecclesiastical writer used testimonies drawn from those books, or anywhere deigned to bring them to memory in his writings.
pass_b_english: Enough on that argument. On to another. The Roman doctors also try to prove that Scripture's authority for us hangs on the Church's from the Church's use and practice.

Apocryphal books, they say, which impostors published under Prophets' and Apostles' names and tried to pass off as sacred, were rejected and exploded by the faithful — and that was by the Church's authority and judgment, which wisely separated those forgeries from the divine books and struck them from the Canon, or at least never judged them receivable.

They pile up Fathers for this. The synopsis attributed to Athanasius, explaining why the Gospels of Thomas, Peter, according to the Hebrews, and the like are not approved, says the Canons of the holy Catholic Church sanctioned four Gospel books for us; besides those it is not safe to have another.

Augustine likewise rejects a Gospel of Thomas the Manichees were offering: We need not believe this Scripture, because it is not in the Catholic Canon; and again, The ecclesiastical Canon rejects these Scriptures. They add Eusebius, who in the Ecclesiastical History often calls such writings Apocrypha because the ancients never mention them, and no church writer cites them or bothers to record them.

lemmas.gloss: from the Church's use and practice
